audience: A lender reviewing a funding request
legal_structure: Assumption: LLC, a common structure for a small U.S. software company. This is not a filed document.
executive_summary: Northwind Studio sells a shared job board so independent design studios can track briefs, files, and approvals in one place. The target customer is studios with 2 to 10 people. Pricing, capital, and the funding amount below are labeled assumptions, not company actuals.
business_concept: A shared job board for briefs, files, and approvals so small studios can stop tracking client work in email and spreadsheets.
competitive_advantage: General work-management tools such as Asana and Monday.com serve many kinds of teams. Northwind Studio is limited to the design-studio workflow of briefs, files, and client approvals.
mission: Give small studios one place to run client work.

values.text: Assumption: only ship features a studio asked for.

objectives.text: Assumption: sign the first ten studios from the founder's existing network within 12 months.

team.name: Amina Rahman
team.background: Named in the context as the founder.

products_and_services: A monthly subscription for the studio, billed per workspace. One job board covers briefs, files, and approvals.
pricing: Assumption: a per-workspace monthly subscription priced against the public plans of Asana and Monday.com.
sourcing: The founder builds and hosts the software. No outside manufacturer is involved.
market_analysis: The target is independent U.S. design studios with 2 to 10 people. Sizing should count establishments in the specialized design services industry from Census business counts and apply the share with 2 to 10 employees.
target_customer: Independent design studios with 2 to 10 people.

competitors.name: Asana
competitors.difference: Asana is general work management for many kinds of teams. Northwind Studio is built only for studio briefs, files, and client approvals.

competitors.name: Monday.com
competitors.difference: Monday.com is a configurable work platform. Northwind Studio ships one fixed studio workflow.

strengths: The founder already works with the studios the first year depends on.
weaknesses: One founder builds, sells, and supports the product.
opportunities: Small studios still track client work in email and spreadsheets.
threats: General work-management tools can add studio templates.
marketing_plan: Direct outreach to studios the founder already works with. Measure studios signed per month.
operations: The founder builds and hosts the software and supports studios directly.
use_of_funds: Assumption: no funding is requested in the first year, so there is no spend plan.

assumptions.text: The first ten studios come from the founder's existing network. The revenue series is sample data that shows the chart shape.

review_cadence: Quarterly while the studio is finding its first customers, and earlier if a competitor launches a studio workflow.
